unitEn: Wake up and rise (childhood and play)
title: ചെമ്പകപ്പൂവ്
author: Rabindranath Tagore (Malayalam translation: K. V. Suresh)
summaryEn:
A small child talks to Amma and imagines a fun game of hide-and-seek. What if I turned into a champak flower (ചെമ്പകപ്പൂവ്, a sweet-smelling yellow flower) at the very top of the champak tree?

All day the child-flower dances in the wind, hides in the leaves, sends out a sweet smell when Amma walks to prayer, and drops a tiny shadow on the book Amma reads after lunch. Amma never guesses it is her child!

In the evening, when Amma goes to the cow shed with her lamp, the flower drops to the ground and becomes her child again, asking for a story. Amma asks, “Where were you?” And the child says: “That's the one thing I can't tell you!”

Big idea: a child's playful imagination and deep love for Amma. The poem was written by the great poet Rabindranath Tagore.

scenes.title: A flower at the top of the tree
sents: അമ്മേ, ആ കാണുന്ന ചെമ്പകത്തിന്റെ നിറുകെയുള്ള കൊമ്പിൽ
Amma, on the very top branch of that champak tree you can see,
suppose I bloomed as a flower, just for fun,
and nodded my head with the soft breeze, and jumped about on top of the new leaves,
and danced — would you be able to tell it was me, Amma?

scenes.title: Hiding in the leaves
sents: Then I will hide a little deeper among the leaves,
എന്റെ ഇതളുകൾ പയ്യെ വിരുത്തി അമ്മ ചെയ്യുന്നതെല്ലാം ഞാൻ നോക്കിക്കാണും.
I will slowly open my petals and watch everything you do, Amma.

scenes.title: A sweet smell on the way to prayer
sents: കുളി കഴിഞ്ഞ്, ഈറൻ മുടിയിഴകൾ ചുമലിലേക്ക് വിതുർത്തിയിട്ട്
After your bath, with your wet hair spread over your shoulders,
when you walk through the champak tree's shade to the little prayer room in our garden,
ഒരു പുതുപൂവിന്റെ മണം തീർച്ചയായും അമ്മ ശ്രദ്ധിക്കും;
you will surely notice the smell of a fresh flower;
without knowing that it is coming from me.

scenes.title: A little shadow on Amma's book
sents: After lunch, at the window that opens onto the garden,
ശിരസ്സിലും മടിയിലും ഈ വൻമരത്തിന്റെ തണൽ പതിപ്പിച്ചുകൊണ്ട്
with the shade of this big tree falling on your head and your lap,
while you sit reading your holy book,
ഞാൻ എന്റെ കുഞ്ഞുനിഴൽ അമ്മ അപ്പോൾ വായിച്ചുകൊണ്ടിരിക്കുന്ന ഏടിലെ
I will drop my tiny shadow onto the very page you are reading,
That little dancing shadow belongs to your own child —
would you be able to tell, Amma?

scenes.title: Back to being Amma's child
sents: കൊളുത്തിപ്പിടിച്ച കൈവിളക്കുമായി, സന്ധ്യയ്ക്ക് അമ്മ പശുത്തൊഴുത്തിലേക്ക് പോകുമ്പോൾ
In the evening, when you go to the cow shed holding a lit hand-lamp,
I will suddenly snap off my stem and drop to the ground,
അമ്മയുടെ പഴയ കുട്ടിയായി മാറി ഒരു കഥ കേൾക്കാനായി വാശിപിടിക്കയും ചെയ്യും.
turn back into your same old child, and keep begging you for a story.
And even then, this is all we will say:
“You naughty one, where have you been all this time?”
“Oh no! That is the one thing I can't tell you, Amma...”

quiz.qe: What does the child imagine becoming?

oe: On the top branch of the champak tree

quiz.qe: What does the child do when Amma calls?
oe: Hides in the leaves and giggles

quiz.qe: What will Amma notice on her way to prayer?
oe: The smell of a fresh flower

quiz.qe: What does Amma do after lunch?
Where will the child drop its tiny shadow?
oe: Between the lines on the page Amma reads

quiz.qe: Where does Amma go in the evening?

quiz.q: പഴയ കുട്ടിയായി മാറിയ ശേഷം കുട്ടി എന്തിനു വാശിപിടിക്കും?
quiz.qe: After becoming a child again, what does the child beg for?

retell: The child imagines becoming a champak flower at the top of the tree, just for fun.
When Amma calls “Where are you?”, the flower hides in the leaves and giggles.
On her way to prayer, Amma smells a fresh flower but doesn't know it is her child.
After lunch, the child drops a tiny shadow on the book Amma is reading.
In the evening the flower falls, becomes a child again and asks for a story.
When Amma asks where it was, the child says: “That I can't tell you!”

write.title: ✍️ If I were a flower...
write.prompt: നീ ഒരു പൂവായി മാറിയാൽ എന്തു ചെയ്യും? എഴുതൂ.
write.en: If you turned into a flower (or anything you like!) for a day, what fun things would you do to surprise your Amma? Write 2–3 sentences. Malayalam, English or mixed is fine.
starters: If I were a flower, I would...
